}</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which element is described by: “An optional line-break position inside long words/URLs.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>&lt;wbr&gt;</code></li><li>B. <code>&lt;dd&gt;</code></li><li>C. <code>&lt;frame&gt;</code></li><li>D. <code>&lt;em&gt;</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p7379">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 7380 / 8000 · Practice 33</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p7381">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p7381" data-page="7381" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 6504"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 33</span><span>Page 7381 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 6504 — var × text-shadow</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">var</span> <span class="badge prop">text-shadow</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">text-shadow</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;var&gt;</code> — a variable in a math expression or program, or a user agent string. Distance above the element (outside its border).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;strike&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><span style="text-decoration:line-through;font-size:13px">Struck text — use <s> or CSS</span></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;strike&gt;Struck text&lt;/strike&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>margin-top</b> = <b>length</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>strike { margin-top: length; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which element is described by: “Japanese/Chinese pinyin-style pronunciation annotation.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>&lt;output&gt;</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>&lt;ruby&gt;</code></li><li>C. <code>&lt;aside&gt;</code></li><li>D. <code>&lt;dd&gt;</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p7388">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 7389 / 8000 · Practice 33</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p7390">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p7390" data-page="7390" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 6513"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 33</span><span>Page 7390 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 6513 — basefont × border</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">basefont</span> <span class="badge prop">border</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">border</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;basefont&gt;</code> — legacy/obsolete element: base font (obsolete). Shorthand: width + style + color for the whole border.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;basefont&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-size:12px">body { font-family: Verdana; font-size: 14px; } — that replaced <basefont></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;basefont face=&quot;Verdana&quot; size=&quot;2&quot;&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>border</b> = <b>1px solid #d1d5db</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>basefont { border: 1px solid #d1d5db; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which element is described by: “Isolates text so its direction does not affect surrounding text.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>&lt;colgroup&gt;</code></li><li>B. <code>&lt;footer&gt;</code></li><li>C. <code>&lt;source&gt;</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>&lt;bdi&gt;</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p7389">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 7390 / 8000 · Practice 33</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p7391">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p7391" data-page="7391" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 6514"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 33</span><span>Page 7391 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 6514 — del × clear</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">del</span> <span class="badge prop">clear</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">clear</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;del&gt;</code> — marks text removed from the document (change tracking). Prevents floats on one or both sides (moves the box below them).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;del&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-size:13px"><del style="color:#9ca3af">Old price: $99</del> → <b>$79</b> <small>(deleted 2026-09-10)</small></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;del datetime=&quot;2026-09-10&quot;&gt;Old price: $99&lt;/del&gt; → $79</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>clear</b> = <b>both</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>del { clear: both; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which element is described by: “A numbered list of items.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>&lt;tbody&gt;</code></li><li>B. <code>&lt;figure&gt;</code></li><li>C. <code>&lt;track&gt;</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>&lt;ol&gt;</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p7390">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 7391 / 8000 · Practice 33</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p7392">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p7392" data-page="7392" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 6515"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 33</span><span>Page 7392 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 6515 — meta × content-visibility</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">meta</span> <span class="badge prop">content-visibility</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">content-visibility</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;meta&gt;</code> — machine-readable metadata about the document (encoding, viewport, description, authors). Skip rendering of off-screen subtrees (auto + contain-intrinsic-size).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;meta&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-family:monospace;font-size:12px;background:#f6f8fa;padding:10px;border:1px solid #d0d7de">charset=UTF-8<br>viewport=width=device-width<br>description="A huge HTML+CSS reference."</div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;meta charset=&quot;UTF-8&quot;&gt; width=&quot;200&quot; height=&quot;80&quot;&gt;&lt;/canvas&gt; &lt;script&gt; const x = document.querySelector(&quot;#c&quot;).getContext(&quot;2d&quot;); x.fillStyle = &quot;#4285f4&quot;; x.fillRect(10, 10, 80, 40); &lt;area shape=&quot;circle&quot; coords=&quot;150,60,30&quot; href=&quot;/lake&quot; alt=&quot;Lake&quot;&gt; &lt;/map&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>transform</b> = <b>none</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>map { transform: none; The main axis direction of a flex container.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;applet&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-size:12px;color:#9ca3af">Java applets: extinct. style=&quot;background:#eef2ff&quot;&gt;&lt;/colgroup&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>cursor</b> = <b>keyword</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>col { cursor: keyword; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which CSS property: “Where the vanishing point sits (x y).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>position</code></li><li>B. <code>font-feature-settings</code></li><li>✔ C. <code>perspective-origin</code></li><li>D. <code>shape-margin</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p7477">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 7478 / 8000 · Practice 34</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p7479">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p7479" data-page="7479" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 6602"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 34</span><span>Page 7479 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 6602 — font × scrollbar-color</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">font</span> <span class="badge prop">scrollbar-color</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">scrollbar-color</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;font&gt;</code> — legacy/obsolete element: font (obsolete). Firefox: scrollbar thumb + track colors.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;font&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><span style="font-family:serif;color:#ef4444;font-size:13px">Legacy: <font> is dead — use CSS</span></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;font face=&quot;Arial&quot; color=&quot;red&quot;&gt;text&lt;/font&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>scrollbar-color</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>font { scrollbar-color: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which CSS property: “Rotation of the element relative to the path (auto follows the tangent).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>left</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>offset-rotate</code></li><li>C. <code>font-variation-settings</code></li><li>D. <code>list-style-position</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p7478">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 7479 / 8000 · Practice 34</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p7480">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p7480" data-page="7480" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 6603"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 34</span><span>Page 7480 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 6603 — acronym × animation-timing-function</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">acronym</span> <span class="badge prop">animation-timing-function</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">animation-timing-function</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;acronym&gt;</code> — legacy/obsolete element: acronym (obsolete). Speed curve per keyframe segment.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;acronym&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><span style="font-size:13px"><abbr title="World Wide Web" style="text-decoration:underline dotted;cursor:help">WWW</abbr> — use <abbr> now</span></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;acronym title=&quot;World Wide Web&quot;&gt;WWW&lt;/acronym&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>animation-timing-function</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>acronym { animation-timing-function: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Matches by class attribute (the workhorse).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>.class</code></li><li>B. <code>:active</code></li><li>C. <code>:empty</code></li><li>D. <code>:in-range / :out-of-range</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p7479">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 7480 / 8000 · Practice 34</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p7481">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p7481" data-page="7481" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 6604"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 34</span><span>Page 7481 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 6604 — nextid × rotate</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">nextid</span> <span class="badge prop">rotate</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">rotate</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;nextid&gt;</code> — legacy/obsolete element: nextid (obsolete). Independent rotate (composes with transform).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;nextid&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-size:12px;color:#9ca3af">No longer in the spec — just use links.</div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;nextid href=&quot;part2.html&quot;&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>rotate</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>nextid { rotate: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Matches when the attribute equals a value (exact, case-sensitive).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:only-child</code></li><li>B. <code>:where(sel, …)</code></li><li>C. <code>:dir(dir)</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>[attr=value]</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p7480">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 7481 / 8000 · Practice 34</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p7482">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p7482" data-page="7482" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 6605"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 34</span><span>Page 7482 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 6605 — html × min-height</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">html</span> <span class="badge prop">min-height</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">min-height</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;html&gt;</code> — the root element of every html document. The lower limit of the height.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;html&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-family:monospace;background:#f6f8fa;padding:10px;border:1px solid #d0d7de">&lt;html&gt; &rarr; &lt;head&gt; + &lt;body&gt;</div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;html lang=&quot;en&quot;&gt; &lt;head&gt;...&lt;/head&gt; &lt;body&gt;...&lt;/body&gt; &lt;/html&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>min-height</b> = <b>0</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>html { min-height: 0; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The value contains the substring.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:first-of-type</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>[attr*=…]</code></li><li>C. <code>:enabled / :disabled</code></li><li>D. <code>+</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p7481">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 7482 / 8000 · Practice 34</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p7483">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p7483" data-page="7483" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 6606"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 34</span><span>Page 7483 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 6606 — script × padding-left</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">script</span> <span class="badge prop">padding-left</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">padding-left</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;script&gt;</code> — embeds or references executable javascript. Inner space at the left.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;script&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-family:monospace;font-size:12px;background:#0d1117;color:#7ee787;padding:10px;border-radius:6px">console.log("hi"); → "hi"</div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;script src=&quot;app.js&quot; defer&gt;&lt;/script&gt; &lt;script&gt; console.log(&quot;hi&quot;); &lt;/script&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>padding-left</b> = <b>length</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>script { padding-left: length; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The element has keyboard/click focus.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:not(sel)</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>:focus</code></li><li>C. <code>:placeholder-shown</code></li><li>D. <code>::after</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p7482">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 7483 / 8000 · Practice 34</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p7484">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p7484" data-page="7484" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 6607"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 34</span><span>Page 7484 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 6607 — aside × outline-offset</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">aside</span> <span class="badge prop">outline-offset</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">outline-offset</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;aside&gt;</code> — content tangentially related to the main content (sidebar, box, pull quote). Distance between the outline and the element edge.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;aside&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="background:#fff3e0;border:1px solid #ffcc80;padding:10px 12px;border-radius:8px;width:230px"><b style="font-size:12px">Did you know?</b><br><span style="font-size:12px">An <b>aside</b> box — related but optional.</span></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;aside&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Did you know?&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt;HTML5 added 40+ new elements.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/aside&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>outline-offset</b> = <b>length</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>aside { outline-offset: length; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “First child of its parent.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:has(sel)</code></li><li>B. <code>:lang(code)</code></li><li>✔ C. <code>:first-child</code></li><li>D. <code>::selection</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p7483">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 7484 / 8000 · Practice 34</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p7485">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p7485" data-page="7485" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 6608"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 34</span><span>Page 7485 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 6608 — figcaption × overflow-y</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">figcaption</span> <span class="badge prop">overflow-y</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">overflow-y</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;figcaption&gt;</code> — the caption for a &lt;figure&gt;. Vertical overflow behavior.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;figcaption&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-size:11px;color:#6b7280;border-top:1px solid #e5e7eb;padding-top:4px;width:250px">Sunrise in Cairo — <i>the figcaption</i></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;figure&gt;&lt;img src=&quot;a.png&quot;&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;Sunrise in Cairo&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>overflow-y</b> = <b>keyword</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>figcaption { overflow-y: keyword; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The n-th child (An+B formulas).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:required / :optional</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>:nth-child(n)</code></li><li>C. <code>descendant (space)</code></li><li>D. <code>::backdrop</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p7484">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 7485 / 8000 · Practice 34</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p7486">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p7486" data-page="7486" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 6609"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 34</span><span>Page 7486 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 6609 — p × align-items</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">p</span> <span class="badge prop">align-items</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">align-items</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;p&gt;</code> — a block of text — the basic unit of written content. Aligns flex items along the cross axis (for all items).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;p&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px;line-height:1.6">A <b>&lt;p&gt;</b> is a paragraph. The browser adds vertical space around it automatically.</p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;This is a paragraph of text.&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>align-items</b> = <b>baseline</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>p { align-items: baseline; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Last of its tag among siblings.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:in-range / :out-of-range</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>:last-of-type</code></li><li>C. <code>::before</code></li><li>D. <code>*</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p7485">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 7486 / 8000 · Practice 34</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p7487">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p7487" data-page="7487" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 6610"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 34</span><span>Page 7487 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 6610 — summary × grid-template-areas</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">summary</span> <span class="badge prop">grid-template-areas</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">grid-template-areas</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;summary&gt;</code> — the visible caption of a &lt;details&gt; disclosure. Names grid regions with an ASCII map — the most readable layout syntax.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;summary&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-size:13px">Click ▸ <b>FAQ</b> to expand — <i>summary is the label</i></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;details&gt;&lt;summary&gt;FAQ&lt;/summary&gt;&lt;p&gt;Answer...&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/details&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>grid-template-areas</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>summary { grid-template-areas: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Matches if ANY listed selector matches (zero specificity!).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:dir(dir)</code></li><li>B. <code>::first-line</code></li><li>C. <code>#id</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>:is(sel, …)</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p7486">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 7487 / 8000 · Practice 34</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p7488">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p7488" data-page="7488" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 6611"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 34</span><span>Page 7488 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 6611 — u × font</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">u</span> <span class="badge prop">font</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">font</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;u&gt;</code> — non-extractive information: a spell-check red line, a signature. Shorthand: font-style font-variant font-weight font-size/line-height font-family.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;u&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px">My name is <u>Ali</u>. — underlined, no meaning</p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;My name is &lt;u&gt;Ali&lt;/u&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>font</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>u { font: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Checkbox/radio is checked.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>:checked</code></li><li>B. <code>+</code></li><li>C. <code>::marker</code></li><li>D. <code>[attr^=…]</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p7487">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 7488 / 8000 · Practice 34</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p7489">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p7489" data-page="7489" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 6612"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 34</span><span>Page 7489 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 6612 — data × letter-spacing</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">data</span> <span class="badge prop">letter-spacing</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">letter-spacing</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;data&gt;</code> — a machine-readable value behind human-readable text. Space between letters (tracking).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;data&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px">Weight: <span title="85">85 kg</span> — value="85" is stored for machines</p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;Weight: &lt;data value=&quot;85&quot;&gt;85 kg&lt;/data&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>letter-spacing</b> = <b>length</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>data { letter-spacing: length; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Value passes / fails validation.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>::after</code></li><li>B. <code>::cue</code></li><li>C. <code>:</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>:valid / :invalid</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p7488">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 7489 / 8000 · Practice 34</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p7490">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p7490" data-page="7490" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 6613"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 34</span><span>Page 7490 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 6613 — sub × vertical-align</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">sub</span> <span class="badge prop">vertical-align</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">vertical-align</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;sub&gt;</code> — subscript text (rendered below the baseline). Shorthand: color + image + position + size + repeat + attachment + origin + clip.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;ul&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><ul style="font-size:13px;margin:0;padding-left:22px;line-height:1.7"><li>HTML</li><li>CSS</li><li>JavaScript</li></ul></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt;HTML&lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;CSS&lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;JavaScript&lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>background</b> = <b>linear-gradient(90deg,#2563eb,#7c3aed)</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>ul { background: linear-gradient(90deg,#2563eb,#7c3aed); }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? Whether the OS &#x27;forced colors&#x27; mode (Windows High Contrast) overrides colors.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;picture&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="display:flex;gap:6px;align-items:center;font-size:11px;font-family:monospace"><span>≤600px → thumb.jpg</span><span>webp → hero.webp</span><span>fallback → hero.jpg</span></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;picture&gt; &lt;source media=&quot;(max-width: 600px)&quot; srcset=&quot;thumb.jpg&quot;&gt; &lt;source type=&quot;image/webp&quot; srcset=&quot;hero.webp&quot;&gt; &lt;img src=&quot;hero.jpg&quot; alt=&quot;Hero&quot;&gt; &lt;/picture&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>forced-color-adjust</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>picture { forced-color-adjust: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? // keyboard document.addEventListener('keydown', function(e){ if(e.target.matches('input,textarea')) return; if(e.key === 'ArrowRight'){ var n = document.querySelector('a[data-nav="next"]'); if(n) n.click(); } if(e.key === 'ArrowLeft'){ var p = document.querySelector('a[data-nav="prev"]'); if(p) p.click(); } }); // jump (every page has one) var boxes = document.querySelectorAll('.jump-input'); for(var bi = 0;
